features.description: Add a package-private request-aware RoundTripper in internal/effects with SEPARATE direct and proxy transport paths (never mutating one shared transport). Per request, http.ProxyFromEnvironment(req) decides: no-proxy => resolveAndValidateIP exactly once then dial that IP with no re-resolution; proxy-selected => ordinary proxy dialing with ZERO local target resolution, and the proxy address never entering the target-IP substitution closure. Route all three Net constructors (net.go:96,212,587) through it. Remove the three preflight resolveAndValidateIP calls (net.go:85,201,565) and the redirect-validator call (:317); validateRedirect keeps count/protocol checks and the caller's cross-origin Authorization stripping but no longer resolves. Preserve public error categories via a typed internal validation error unwrapped through *url.Error - the two makeResultErr("Transport", ...) sites to update are net.go:567 (moved preflight) and net.go:631 (post-client.Do, url.Error-wrapped).
acceptance_criteria: AC-M1.1 (doc M1 AC1): `go test -count=1 ./internal/effects -run 'TestNetProxyBoundary|TestNetProxyDirectPin|TestNetProxyNoProxy|TestNetProxyRedirectControls' -v` passes outside the sandbox. BASE AT 945f36727: rc=0, '=== RUN' count = 0, '[no tests to run]' - VACUOUSLY GREEN. Pass requires ALL THREE: rc=0 AND '=== RUN' count >= 4 AND a '--- PASS' line per named test. Tests must use a target whose DNS answer/dial endpoint differs from the fake proxy and assert the OBSERVED dial/CONNECT destination. SILENT-REVERT CHECK: reverting production routing makes the fake proxy observe no request, or makes the old pinning closure dial the target - either reds; deleting the tests drops '=== RUN' to 0 and reds.

AC-M1.2 (doc M1 AC2): a direct/NO_PROXY subtest asserts the accepted connection reaches the INJECTED VALIDATED IP, not the request hostname's alternate endpoint. BASE: no such test exists; new by construction. SILENT-REVERT CHECK: replacing both paths with ordinary proxy/default dialing fails the endpoint assertion; removing NO_PROXY handling routes the request to the fake proxy and reds.

AC-M1.3 (doc M1 AC3): capability denial, initial-domain rejection, redirect-protocol rejection, and redirect-count rejection each run WITH A PROXY SELECTED, and the injected resolver counter stays EXACTLY 0 for proxy-selected initial AND redirect requests. SILENT-REVERT CHECK: restoring preflight/redirect resolution increments the counter and reds; deleting proxy support makes the proxy-positive arm fail and reds.

AC-M1.4 (doc M1 AC4): direct-route DNS/IP rejection tests assert EXACTLY 1 resolver call, EXACTLY 0 dial calls, and the existing legacy E_NET_DNS_FAILED / E_NET_IP_BLOCKED or structured Err(Transport, ...) category as applicable. Category source of truth (V20, re-verified at 945f36727): E_NET_IP_BLOCKED at net_security.go:27,34,46,51,56; E_NET_DNS_FAILED at :90,94. SILENT-REVERT CHECK: double resolution fails the call count; ordinary dialing fails the zero-dial assertion; losing url.Error unwrapping fails the exact-category assertion.

MILESTONE BOUNDARY (all rc=0 at base, must remain rc=0): `go build ./internal/effects/... ./internal/executor/... ./internal/testutil/...`; `go test -count=1 ./internal/effects`; `go vet ./internal/effects`.
risks: Pin closure rewrites the PROXY address (doc's top risk) - mitigated by separate per-mode transports plus AC-M1.1's observed-dial-endpoint assertion
